name: OPPO Hyper Legend Cup
desc: A Discord bot for the 2026 OPPO Hyper Legend Cup x MLBB Campus Series. It checks players against the team registration sheet, runs the support desk, schedules announcements and records match results.

p: The 2026 OPPO Hyper Legend Cup x MLBB Campus Series is a university Mobile Legends: Bang Bang tournament that OPPO ran across Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines. The OPPO event page lists registration from 16 to 28 February, online qualifiers on 7 and 14 March, and a cross-national final in Kuala Lumpur in April. The Philippine side of it lived in a Discord server, and that server needed to tell real registered players from everyone else, answer questions from teams, and keep match results straight on the days that mattered.
I built the bot for that server. The code is in a public repository, and the history runs from 12 February to 7 March 2026.

Most of the bot's skeleton went in on the first day. The initial commit already had seven cogs, 16 slash commands and a MySQL database started through Docker Compose. The same day added a GitHub Action that restarts the bot server on every push to main, and a check of player details against a Google Sheet.

That check is the core of verification. A player clicks Verify, reads a guide image showing where to find their UID and server ID in the game, and fills in both numbers in a form. The bot looks the pair up in the registration sheet, which it reads as a CSV export of a view-only Google Sheet and caches for five minutes. On a match it assigns the player's role, renames them to team abbreviation and in-game name, stores the record and sends a confirmation DM. A command drops the cache and refetches when the sheet changes.

The sheet parser only reads player rows, so coaches and managers got their own button on 5 March. They pick Coach or Manager, enter a staff code, and give a team name that has to exist in the sheet. The bot allows one coach and one manager per team. League Ops staff who weren't in the sheet at all are handled by a manual entry list that the verification form falls back to.

Verification, tickets and embeds all run through one bot, with MySQL behind it. Verifying assigns a role and a nickname. Closing a ticket sends the player a transcript and a five-star rating prompt by DM. Embeds come from Discohook links and can be scheduled for a later time.

Players open a ticket in one of four categories: League Ops, Technical, Creatives or General. Each ticket is a private channel visible to the role that owns the category. Staff claim tickets (a player can't claim their own), and an unclaimed ticket pings its role after 24 hours and escalates after 48. A background check runs every 10 minutes for that. On close the bot builds an HTML transcript, posts it to a log channel and DMs it to the player along with the rating prompt. Pending ratings are stored in the database, so a restart doesn't lose them.

Announcements are built in Discohook, a web editor for Discord embeds. Pasting its link into a command sends the embed, and an optional date and time, read as UTC+8, schedules it. Scheduled embeds sit in MySQL and get picked up again after a restart. Separate commands create up to 50 private threads at once with retry on rate limits, and post a role mention into every thread of a channel. A trigger voice channel spawns a personal channel for whoever joins and deletes it when it empties.
The match tools arrived last. On 28 February I added match sessions and a Challonge integration, and most of the rest followed between 4 and 7 March.

A marshal opens a session for two teams with a best-of count, optionally starts a 15 minute grace period before a game, and logs each game result. After every result the bot opens a five minute window where each team's players type an acknowledgement. Anyone can file a dispute, which pauses the clock until a marshal or admin resolves it. If five minutes of undisputed time pass, the bot acknowledges for both teams and the result stands. Sessions, games and acknowledgements are written to the database as they happen, and the bot reloads open sessions on startup, so a restart mid-match doesn't lose the score.

Challonge links a bracket to a channel, lists its matches and reports a result through a guided flow of prompts. Three log channels record command use, tickets and embeds. A help command shows only the commands the person asking is allowed to run.
I don't have a number for how the bot did on the day, and the repository doesn't hold one. What's there is the code and the commit history.
